newsitem.title: USA: Warmth aids Illinois crops, corn harvest begins.
newsitem.headline: Warmth aids Illinois crops, corn harvest begins.

text.p: Illinois corn and soybean development progressed well during the week ended Sunday because of warm weather and some rain, said the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.
Corn harvest was in its early stages in the southern half of the state and elsewhere in the state it was drying quickly.
Crop development was about two weeks behind the average and soybeans needed more rain and warm weather to promote growth and pod filling.

Two percent of the soybeans were dropping leaves versus five a year ago and the 16 average. Fourteen percent of the crop had turned yellow versus 21 a year ago and the 43 average. Soybeans were rated four percent excellent, 35 good, 37 fair, 17 poor and seven very poor.

About eight percent of the corn was mature versus 16 a year ago and the 30 average. About 56 had dented versus 75 a year ago and the 76 average. The crop was rated 10 percent excellent, 41 good, 32 fair, 12 poor and five very poor.
Sorghum was three percent mature versus one a year ago and the 14 average.
Topsoil moisture was rated 28 percent adequate, 48 short and 24 very short.
